visual_brief.subject: A compact forecasting model that turns observed temporal history into a calibrated range of possible futures
verified_context: Timestral is a family of four downloadable time-series foundation models ranging from 5 million to 209 million parameters.
The models forecast related series jointly and emit 21 quantiles rather than one point estimate.
They support past-only, known-future, and categorical covariates with up to 32,768 time steps of context and CPU or GPU inference.
visual_brief.editorial_idea: A small specialist instrument can preserve uncertainty by expanding one observed history into a structured fan of plausible futures.
visual_brief.visual_metaphor: Layered time ribbons pass through a compact brass-and-stone observation instrument and emerge as a restrained fan of translucent paper bands.

candidate_notes.A: Constitution-compliant. The constructed instrument is credible and the fan is clear, but the symmetric laboratory framing feels less editorial than the selected composition.
candidate_notes.B: Selected. The compact instrument and broad nested paper fan make uncertainty the focal phenomenon, with strong negative space and no invented data language.
candidate_notes.C: Constitution-compliant. The landscape textures add material richness, though they compete slightly with the forecasting metaphor.
